mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a quarter signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of falling unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) over two consecutive quarters signals strong consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising PCE.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong labor market indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high interest rates and rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% in a quarter and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 0.5% in the same period, it signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of weak GDP growth and declining industrial production.
